These pages are expositions of published methods without Lean formalization; each names the…
nodes.title: Attention and low-rank adaptation

nodes.summary: Bayes' rule and conjugate models, expectation-maximization for mixtures and latent-variable models, variational mean-field inference, and Monte Carlo, rejection, Gibbs and Metropolis-Hastings sampling. Bayesian nonparametric priors (the Dirichlet process and urn schemes) are under Bayesian statistics.
nodes.title: Bayesian inference and sampling

nodes.summary: Linear algebra of diffusion and flow-based generative models: for Gaussian data, the score and the optimal denoiser are spectral functions of the data covariance and the probability-flow ODE is a linear system with commuting coefficients whose flow map is an explicit affine map; for any differentiable velocity field, the divergence in the log-density computations of flow models is the trace of a Jacobian. nodes.summary: Uniform deviation bounds between the empirical and the expected risk, obtained from concentration inequalities: for a finite class, Hoeffding's inequality and a union bound; for a general class, McDiarmid's bounded-differences inequality concentrates the supremum of the deviations around its mean. These pages are AI-authored expositions of published results without Lean formalization; each names what it relies on,…
nodes.title: Generalization bounds and concentration

nodes.summary: Linear algebra of recent state-space sequence layers such as Mamba and Mamba-2: for fixed parameters, a linear time-varying state-space recurrence acts along the sequence as multiplication by a semiseparable matrix, and a time-invariant one as a lower-triangular Toeplitz matrix, that is, a causal convolution. These pages are expositions of published results without Lean formalization; each names the linear algebra…
nodes.title: Linear state-space sequence models

nodes.summary: Mistake and regret bounds for sequential prediction: perceptron, weighted majority, Hedge (multiplicative weights) and AdaBoost.
nodes.title: Online learning and boosting

nodes.summary: Bayesian networks and their Markov properties, structure scores and Markov equivalence, causal networks and adjustment, belief propagation and variable elimination, conditional random fields, hidden Markov models (forward-backward, Viterbi, Baum-Welch) and the Kalman filter.
nodes.title: Probabilistic graphical models

nodes.summary: Prediction from labelled data: least squares, ridge, lasso and kernel or Gaussian-process regression (including GBLUP), the bias-variance decomposition, Bayes classifiers and optimal predictors, log loss, decision-tree information gain, backpropagation, and sufficient input subsets. nodes.summary: Structure in unlabelled data: k-means, archetypal analysis, nonnegative matrix factorization, the successive projection algorithm, and probabilistic PCA with the Gaussian factor-analysis marginal. Classical principal component analysis is under linear models and multivariate analysis.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
